_doc: Words the player reads. Rule: one or two short sentences per line, a speaker on every line, nothing longer than a breath. Lore notes are optional reading.
intro: Three hundred years ago, the sun went out.
Tallow lives under the last Great Lantern. Tonight, for seven heartbeats, it went dark.
Something came over the wall in those seven heartbeats. It took a child.
You are the Ninth Lamplighter. The other eight are dead or missing. Go.

captions.arrive: The Glasswood. It was a forest, once.
captions.first_dark: Outside your light, the Dusk hits harder. Keep it fed.
captions.first_level: The lantern burns brighter for you. Spend your points (K, P).
captions.lamp_lit: The waylamp holds. This ground remembers the light.
captions.relight_start: Hold the lamp until it catches. The dark will come for it.
captions.boss: The stone ring. Something tall stands among the stones, and it is holding a child made of glass.
captions.slice_end: End of the test slice. Nim is home. The Dusk is not done with Tallow.

ysolde.name: Captain Ysolde Marr
lines: Ysolde
Seven heartbeats of dark and the Glasswood came knocking. They took Nim Saltry off the wall-walk.
Ysolde
I'd send soldiers. Soldiers don't come back from the Dusk. Lamplighters sometimes did.
Ysolde
Light the old waylamps as you go. Each one is a place the dark has to remember to fear.
Ysolde
And if you meet something that talks... don't let it finish its sentences.
repeat: Gate stays shut until you're back. With her.

hask.name: Hask
lines: Hask
Easy with the light, Lamplighter. I'm only half of what you'd be hitting.
Hask
The girl? The Glazier took her to the stone ring. It collects things that shine.
Hask
Ask yourself why the Dusk wanted a child who maps the wall. Then don't ask me.
Hask
Your predecessor asked better questions. Look where it got him. Cairn by the deer trail.
repeat: Still here. Still half. Go on.

nim.name: Nim Saltry
lines: Nim
You took your time. I counted. Four thousand one hundred heartbeats.
Nim
It kept asking where the Lantern's heart is. I lied. I'm very good at lying.
Nim
Lamplighter... it wasn't angry. It was scared. Of you. Of that lantern.
repeat: Walk me home? I know a shortcut. It's mostly screaming.

teague_cairn.title: A note under a cold lantern
lines: If you're reading this, Ottilie sent you. She lies when she's frightened.
Ask her what the Great Lantern burns. Watch her hands when she answers.
— T. Morrow, Eighth

brennick.title: Old Brennick, still fishing
lines: A woodcutter, turned to glass where he sat. His line still hangs in the water.
Tied to the rod, a child's note: 'Da. I bring you tea on Tuesdays. Come home when the fish bite.'

order_rules.title: A page from a Lamplighter's cache
lines: Rule one: never look into the shard.
Rule two: it is not a stone.
Rule three: if it speaks, it is dreaming. Do not answer.

signs.road: Tallow  -  Glasswood Road  -  (someone scratched: TURN BACK)
